root_motivation: A chain step naming a host.* verb publishes and dry-runs green today, then fails tool_not_found on every real fire: compose_call only resolves a step against the tenant's own tools table, never the host.*/billing.* dispatcher handler.rs's ~150-arm match actually uses. On 2026-09-30 this cost one full build round on the fleet-board dogfood chain, and the quickstart's own chain example names two tools (fetch_rows/write_rows) that exist nowhere, so every agent that follows it hits the same failure.
user_persona: A workflow-orchestrator agent composing a fetch/transform/persist pipeline whose last step is a host.* write; a first-hour agent following host.quickstart kind=chain; an operator who wants a chain step barred from naming a destructive control-plane verb.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a chain whose step 2 is {"tool":"host.table.append","args":{"table":"runs","rows":"$.prev.result.rows"}}, When published and called with input that step 1 turns into one row, Then the run status is done, steps[1].result.appended == 1, and host.table.query returns the row.

Given a chain spec whose step names a bare tool that does not exist in the tenant, When host.spec_test or host.tool_publish runs, Then the error class is step_tool_not_found, data.step is the index, data.name the string, and nothing is published.
Given a chain spec whose step names host.tool_remove, When published, Then the error class is step_tool_not_allowed and data.allowed equals the allowlist returned by host.quickstart kind=chain.

Given a published chain with a host.table.append step, When host.tool_test runs it, Then the dry-run report lists the step as resolved: host and, once PRD-mcphost-dry-run-side-effects has landed, no row is written; before that, the report carries side_effects: true for that step.

Given host.quickstart kind=chain, When its steps[0].arguments.spec is passed to host.spec_test unchanged on a tenant that published the quickstart's python starter, Then spec_test passes with every step resolved.
Given a chain with one host step, When called once, Then host.usage by=tool shows one call for the chain and the calls row carries step_tool: "host.table.append".
Given a free-plan tenant at table_rows_max, When a chain's host.table.append step would exceed it, Then the run fails at that step with the same error class a direct host.table.append call returns.

Given the landed binary deployed on prod and tenant joe-test's webhook trigger fleet_ingest retargeted at a chain whose second step is host.table.append, When ~/.local/bin/fleet-post manual chainhost-live fleet-board-verify webhook gate runs from orch, Then within 60s host.table.query on runs returns a row with run_id = 'chainhost-live' and host.runs.get for the hook's run shows status: done with the host step resolved: host.

additional.test_file_names_use_test_prefix_chainhos: test_prefix chainhost (the PRD's own frontmatter field): tests/chainhost_ac<NN>_<slug>.rs, same convention as every other test file in this repo.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does compose_call need a second resolution path (HOST_STEPS_ALLOWED) instead of just adding host.* rows to the tenant's own tools table?
five_whys_trace.a: host.* verbs are dispatched by handler.rs's dispatch_tenant_tool, a fixed ~150-arm match over control-plane logic, not by a Kind::call against a stored spec -- there is no spec to store a tools-table row around, so a step naming one has to reach that dispatcher directly.

five_whys_trace.q: Why resolve every step's tool at publish/spec_test time (resolve_steps) rather than only at call time (compose_call's own narrower lookup)?
five_whys_trace.a: This PRD's own grounding incident is exactly a chain that published and dry-ran green with an unresolvable step, discovered only when a real trigger fired -- resolving at publish time turns that into an immediate refusal instead of a silent landmine.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does TenantHostStepBridge always pass subject: None and auth_method: "key" rather than re-deriving the chain run's own caller identity?
five_whys_trace.a: Of every allowlisted verb, only host.whoami (not on the allowlist) ever reads either parameter, so there is nothing a chain step loses by not re-deriving them; end_user and calls_auth_method (what the allowlisted verbs actually meter by) are threaded through from the chain's own real call.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is step_tool a single-slot Mutex cell on TenantHostStepBridge, read back after kind.call returns, rather than a field CallCtx carries directly?
five_whys_trace.a: Same shape CellResourceSink already uses for cpu_ms/peak_rss_kb: the value is only known once the chain's own step dispatch actually runs, and the one calls row call_published_tool writes needs to read it back after kind.call returns, not before.

five_whys_trace.q: Why keep record_call_attributed_with_end_user as a separate wrapper instead of adding step_tool directly to it?
five_whys_trace.a: Same 'existing call sites don't all need a trailing None' rationale every prior wrapper in that chain already documents -- record_call_attributed_with_end_user_and_step_tool is the fifth layer, not a breaking change to the fourth.

ambiguities_resolved.question: When a chain has more than one host step, which one does calls.step_tool (AC6) record?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The last one dispatched -- TenantHostStepBridge.step_tool is a single-slot cell overwritten on each host dispatch, same 'last writer wins' shape CellResourceSink already uses for cpu_ms/peak_rss_kb. Requirement 6 and AC6 only exercise a chain with exactly one host step; no landed chain spec has more than one yet.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does a host step's own dispatch (dispatch_tenant_tool) write its own calls row, double-counting host.usage by=tool?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- dispatch_tenant_tool's match arms call the control-plane business logic directly (tables::table_append, tenant_state::state_set, etc.), never call_published_tool, so a host step writes no calls row of its own; the chain's own one row (tool_name = the chain) is the only one, satisfying AC6's 'shows one call for the chain' as-is.
